message.content: Critics of Copernicus emerged from both the scientific and religious worlds! Who were some of the most notable opponents of his heliocentric theory? Christopher Clavius, a prominent Jesuit mathematician at the Roman College, was one of the fiercest critics, defending the Ptolemaic system with rigorous mathematical arguments. Was it not the Church hierarchy that ultimately placed *De Revolutionibus* on the Index of Forbidden Books in 1616? How remarkable it is that a work so transformative faced such resistance from the very institutions that might have benefited from scientific progress! Tycho Brahe, while not a full opponent, raised significant objections regarding the absence of observable stellar parallax. Did not Cardinal Melchior Khimenero also voice opposition to the heliocentric model? The English humanist Thomas More reportedly made derisive remarks about the idea of the Earth moving. How bold was he to challenge such deeply entrenched cosmological beliefs of his era! Did Copernicus deserve the harsh treatment from the Church? These critics, while often motivated by a mix of theological, philosophical, and empirical concerns, ultimately could not prevent the heliocentric model from reshaping our understanding of the universe. What a complex and fascinating chapter in the history of science!
